how_to_resume: 1. Read education/README.md, then ARCHITECTURE.md and METHODOLOGY.md.
3. Read this file's `current_area` and `next_areas`, then continue from there.
4. Anything in `discovered_concepts_unresearched` is fair game and already has provenance.
5. Anything in `unresolved_historical_claims` needs a primary source before it can be stated.
6. Respect `tool_limitations` — those are known dead ends, not untried ideas.

unresolved_historical_claims.claim: The rule that stalemate is a draw was not universal historically; it has been scored as a win and as a loss in various times and places.
unresolved_historical_claims.needed: Primary or scholarly sources on regional stalemate conventions before standardisation.

unresolved_historical_claims.claim: FIDE formerly granted exceptions to the fifty-move rule for specific endgames later shown by tablebase to require more than 50 moves, and removed them.
unresolved_historical_claims.needed: The specific FIDE handbook editions that added and removed the exception list.

failed_research_attempts.reason: JS-heavy tag-archive page; content came from Exa search highlights instead

failed_research_attempts.what: Stockfish depth-34 multipv-3 analysis of the Kotov-Pachman move-55 rook ending
failed_research_attempts.result: no convergence in 16 minutes; killed to free CPU
failed_research_attempts.reason: simplified rook endings explode at high depth; cap at 28-30 or use tablebase

failed_research_attempts.what: Controlled pair for Nimzowitsch's open-file condition on outposts
failed_research_attempts.reason: The 'closed file' half was built by adding a white pawn on d3, which also added a pawn of material (+0.52 -> +2.22 baseline). The halves were not comparable. Retest by relocating the c2 pawn to d3 so material is identical.

failed_research_attempts.what: Controlled pair for the outpost's 'cannot be challenged by a pawn' condition
failed_research_attempts.result: inconclusive — variable could not be isolated
failed_research_attempts.reason: Moving Black's c-pawn c7->c5 made d5 unchallengeable as intended, but also made d6 backward and opened b5. Nb5 became +2.47 while Nd5 fell to last at +0.93. Side effects swamped the tested variable.

failed_research_attempts.what: Corrected relocation pair (c2->d3) for Nimzowitsch's open-file condition
failed_research_attempts.reason: Material was correctly held constant, but all four candidate moves fell within 0.08 of each other. The result ran mildly opposite to Nimzowitsch's prediction, which is noise rather than evidence. A discriminating position is needed, not a quieter one.

failed_research_attempts.what: Greek Gift controlled pair at depth 28 with MultiPV 4, and the breakthrough pair at depth 34, run concurrently
failed_research_attempts.result: neither converged in ~12 minutes; both killed and rerun at depth 20/26
failed_research_attempts.reason: Two compounding mistakes. (1) MultiPV disables most pruning, so a MultiPV search on a 28-piece middlegame costs far more than a single-PV search to the same depth — depth 20-22 is ample for a question whose answer is a forced sequence. (2) sf_analyse.py defaults threads to cpu_count-2 = 10, so two concurrent runs requested 20 threads on 12 cores and thrashed. Run engine jobs SEQUENTIALLY, or pass --threads.

failed_research_attempts.what: Two background waiter shells left polling for sentinels that could never appear
failed_research_attempts.result: orphaned; they would have spun forever
failed_research_attempts.reason: When the over-deep Stockfish runs were killed, sf_analyse.py raised BrokenPipeError writing `quit` to the dead engine. That escaped and killed the wrapping shell script BEFORE it echoed its DONE sentinel, so the `until grep -q DONE...` waiters had nothing to wait for. The results themselves were fine — obtained by reruns and already incorporated — but the waiters were unrecoverable.

failed_research_attempts.item: controlled pair isolating king activity in a rook ending
failed_research_attempts.detail: Two designs tried, both failed to split. Pair 1 (defending king e7 vs a7 in R+P vs R) came out win/win, though with dtm 35 vs 15, which was kept as a measurement of defensive value. Pair 2 (Philidor setup, defending king e7 vs g7) came out draw/draw - the rook on the sixth holds regardless of the king's square. Consistent with the three failed outpost pairs and with Shereshevsky's own remark that rook endings are too concrete for the principle to isolate.
failed_research_attempts.conclusion: Recorded on the king-activation concept as a limitation; the concept claims only what the win/win pair measured.

limits: Piping all UCI commands at once and closing stdin makes it read `quit` mid-search and exit before printing any info line — it returns a bestmove with no evaluation and LOOKS like it worked. tools/sf_analyse.py streams and waits for `bestmove`.
Simplified endgames can fail to converge at depth 34+. Prefer tablebase below 8 pieces.
Two concurrent instances halve each other's throughput on this 12-core machine.

MultiPV is expensive: it suppresses pruning, so multipv 3-4 at depth 28 on a full board can take an order of magnitude longer than depth 28 single-PV. For forced-sequence questions depth 20-22 with MultiPV is plenty.
education/tools/sf_analyse.py defaults to cpu_count-2 threads. Two concurrent invocations oversubscribe the machine. Run jobs sequentially in one script.
FIXED: sf_analyse.py used to raise BrokenPipeError if the engine died mid-search, killing the calling script. It now tolerates a dead pipe and raises a clear RuntimeError naming the problem instead.
7 pieces maximum. Above that, engine analysis is the only option.
Network dependent; tools/tablebase.py retries three times then records wdl 'unknown'.
tvly extract returns site chrome and JSON-wrapped raw_content that needs stripping.
Search can rank a SUPERSEDED FIDE Laws PDF above the current one — verify edition dates.
tvly research takes 3-5 minutes and pads its source count with index pages.
Highlights are excerpts and can stitch together non-adjacent text; fetch the page before quoting anything as continuous prose.
Installed only in a scratchpad venv, not a project dependency. Repo tools must not require it; it is used optionally for SAN rendering and legality checks.
Works on tactical motifs, which depend on one geometric relation.

Does NOT work on positional concepts: no pawn can be moved without changing several structural facts simultaneously. Three separate designs failed on the outpost. Use annotated real positions plus recognition criteria instead, and do not mark positional concepts 'validated' on controlled-pair evidence.

tool_limitations.tool: background shell scripts (Bash run_in_background + until-loop waiters)
limits: A waiter polling for a sentinel is only safe if the producing script writes that sentinel UNCONDITIONALLY. If a step raises, the script dies before the echo and the waiter spins forever. Use `trap 'echo DONE_X' EXIT` at the top of the script, not a bare echo at the bottom.
Renaming or rerunning an analysis under a different output filename orphans any waiter still watching the old one. Kill the waiter or reuse the filename.
Orphaned waiters are harmless — idle sleep loops — but they are invisible in ps output unless you grep for the loop body rather than for the analysis tool.

tool_limitations.note: theoretical-novelty, tabiya and gambit identification all require a game database the Education System does not have. Recorded on each concept as a limitation rather than left for a caller to discover.

measurements.what: How many of the 788 shipped puzzle `why` cards name a motif in chess vocabulary
measurements.conclusion: Quantifies the Education System's surface. The tactical single-move case is covered at 88-100% by findMotifs() and puzzle_words.js and cannot be improved on by this project. The quiet/structural case is at 4-38%, and overall a third of all cards contain no chess vocabulary at all. Research priority is therefore positional, not tactical.

measurements.method: Controlled searchmoves comparison: Stockfish 18, depth 26, 10 threads, 2048MB. For each position every candidate was evaluated inside ONE search of that position, so the only variable is the move. This avoids the separate-search artefacts that make cross-position gambit comparisons unreliable.
findings: Gambit compensation is a measurable quantity, and it can be complete: the Evans Gambit is a pawn down and evaluates to exactly 0.00, so what is surrendered is White's opening edge (0.28) rather than the pawn.

Compensation must be established per gambit, never inferred from the word: the Halloween Gambit gives a knight for a pawn and measures 1.75 worse than the best move, with visible activity and no adequate compensation.
The 'don't bring the queen out early' rule is confirmed in direction and is smaller than its usual phrasing implies: 2.Qh5 costs 0.68 against 2.Nf3.

The claim that the King's Gambit is simply unsound is only partly supported. 2.f4 concedes 0.91 relative to 2.Nf3, which is an inferior line rather than a refuted one - and it evaluates BELOW 2.Qh5, the move beginners are told never to play.

Methodological: openings are one of the few positional areas where controlled comparison is easy, because the alternatives are all legal moves in a single position. This is the same searchmoves technique that failed to isolate outposts, and it works here for exactly that reason.
